canonical_statement: The study developed and clinically evaluated an RNA-based NAAT intended to distinguish active toxigenic C. difficile infection from colonization by detecting organism RNA and toxin-gene RNA expression.

canonical_statement: The multiplex RNA-NAAT targeted C. difficile 23S rRNA for organism detection, tcdA and tcdB transcripts for toxin A/B expression, cdtB for binary toxin expression, and BactQuant 16S rRNA as a bacterial extraction control.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: RNA-NAAT primers and probes targeting the 23S ribosomal RNA (rRNA) were designed to specifically detect the presence of C. diff

canonical_statement: Each extracted clinical sample was tested in paired RT-PCR reactions, one with reverse transcriptase heat-inactivated at 95°C for 5 minutes, so an upward Ct shift in the heat-inactivated reaction could indicate target RNA.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Each extracted sample was run in duplicate; one sample was incubated at 95⁰C for 5 minutes to inactivate reverse transcriptase.

canonical_statement: RNA-NAAT classified toxigenic C. difficile when 23S rRNA and toxin-gene targets were positive; toxin RNA expression required a tcdA/tcdB ΔCt shift greater than 1.5.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: only samples showing a ΔCt shift greater than 1.5 for tcdA/tcdB targets were deemed positive for RNA expression

canonical_statement: Every clinical sample was evaluated by RNA-NAAT, GDH EIA, toxin EIA, DNA-NAAT, a forward EIA-to-NAAT two-step algorithm, and a reverse NAAT-to-EIA two-step algorithm.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: evaluate the clinical performance of RNA-NAAT relative to 5 currently available commercial diagnostic strategies (3 individual tests plus two reflex algorithms)

canonical_statement: The institutional standard-of-care forward two-step algorithm used joint GDH/toxin EIA first and reflex DNA-NAAT for discordant antigen/toxin results.
